page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-8-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine offering 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8481C processor clocked at 2.7 GHz, coupled with 32 GB of system memory. Operating on the x86_64 architecture with 2 threads per core, it features a 105 MB L3 cache along with hardware instruction support for AVX-512, AMX tile, and AMX INT8 vector and matrix processing. The configuration contains no dedicated GPUs, preserving an even 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM memory density.

A key feature of the c3-standard-8-lssd configuration is the inclusion of 804 GB of local NVMe SSD storage across two drives. Unlike diskless instances that rely solely on external network-attached block storage, the integrated NVMe storage offers direct-attached, low-latency disk input and output, catering to processes that require high-throughput temporary or scratch storage directly on the hypervisor node.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent median-tier performance across general compute and memory-bound tasks. The instance records a Geekbench multi-core score of 6546.0, a PassMark CPU score of 11820.18, and uncached large-block memory read throughput of 55.2 GB/sec. Operational benchmarks highlight steady throughput in transactional operations, reaching 8.89 million Redis SET operations per second and 13.23 GB/sec in static web serving. Lower-tier performance appears in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 35.19 GB/sec and 7B-parameter LLM generation at 7.69 tokens per second, indicating scaling boundaries under heavy parallel CPU stress.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides balanced compute and memory capacity without requiring external storage overhead for high-IOPS local caching or temporary tables. The c3-standard-8-lssd is suitable for transactional database servers, in-memory data caching, static web hosting, and containerized backend workloads requiring fast local storage.
